additional_info.subject: 0411096 - ID0411096-DC/Si-D/DE[Energu] - BCB toggle hotfix CRM:00315002424
additional_info.body:
Hello Martin,
Thank you again for your time and availability to test this scenario.
From our tests we see that the BCB toggle or Wake-up function is working but with a few hiccups along the way.
Steps need to be taken to make the BCB toggle occur:
Start the charging session with Volvo
Stop the charging session via button next to the CCS socket.
Confirm in HMI the session is completed (Press “Finished”)
Wait for the timeout when the screen shows “please unplug the vehicle” until the Logout is completed.
Select the DC outlet being used in the HMI and present the RFID card when requested.
“Connection Failed” message on the screen
Wait for the session to resume as this looks like a bug (5-10sec).
The truck starting charging again as we expected.
We will align with R&D for the following questions:
If the timeout of the “please unplug” can be skipped since it's not really the case here.
“Connection Failed” message fix.
Find a way to skip the need to present the RFID physically, since the use case for the BCB is for the truck to wake-up the charger automatically, when it wants to restart the charging process.
For example, if we want to leave the truck charging for the whole night and have it full by the morning.
An email will follow up after this one for the IVECO issue we found so that we are not mixing up topics.
Thank you very much again!
Best regards,
Francisco

Here is my analysis from the IVECO truck starting issue. I will share a comparison between the Volvo FHE and the IVECO for you to bring this to IVECO's attention.
Working session with Volvo:
SECC logs:
PCAP logs:
After this V2G SDP Request (SECC Discovery Protocol=SDP) the session runs as expected.
Non-working session with IVECO:
SECC logs:
PCAP logs:
There is no SDP request and as such he stays stuck in Link Status request, until here:
Since it doesn't establish a V2G communication, we are not able to go even to Authentication.
As we already tested, it was possible to be a CCS issue since I've faced a similar behaviour, but we tried at least 5 sessions with DC2 and Volvo, and everytime it worked perfectly.
When we used the same CCS for the IVECO it never worked, so from our side it's clear that there is nothing wrong with the cable.
I hope this information is enough to work with IVECO, please let me know if you have any feedback from them and let's continue working together.
Thank you again as always.
Best regards,
Francisco
